name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: Colin Allred's large fundraising advantage and name recognition
Open seat after Crockett's retirement, but seat stays with the incumbent party
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near certainty
model.rationale: The D+18 district fundamentals make this a Safe Democratic hold even with Crockett off the ballot, and Allred's $7.4 million war chest and high profile dwarf an underfunded Republican opponent. Markets price the race at roughly 97% Democratic, consistent with the fundamentals.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Gillespie or an unexpectedly strong Republican national environment could narrow the margin, though a flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jasmine Crockett's retirement leaves this Dallas-area district open, but the seat remains firmly in Democratic hands on paper. The district carries an 18-point Democratic partisan lean, and Democrats have a strong nominee in Colin Allred, a former congressman and 2024 Senate candidate who has raised over $7 million. Republican Patrick Gillespie has reported minimal fundraising and little outside support.

Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee at roughly a 97% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. The main question is the size of the margin rather than the outcome, with the open-seat transition and Allred's low cash-on-hand the only mild sources of uncertainty.
